symptom: The public application intermittently replaced a requested business page with the shared route error boundary and, in a fresh browser, returned a 500 Internal server error.
expected_behavior: Public pages render verified content through cold loads, reloads and route transitions, and a release change cannot pair an old rendered document with new hashed assets.
environment: vii.spaplus.co on 3 November 2026; public baseline Version appgver_87cf0f1a04608191b067d46435fde5e8 and cumulative candidate starting at commit 0f744df409a4b901000b3052400f22caa4b9dd4b.

steps: Open https://vii.spaplus.co/business?id=vacation-164 in a fresh browser context.
Observe the document response and visible title and body.
Repeat the same route through direct HTTP probes.
reproduction.evidence: The browser showed title This site ran into a problem and body 500 Internal server error. Six immediate HTTP repeats then returned 200 with 2.7 to 7.6 second latency, proving an intermittent runtime failure.

observations.observation: The current public service worker uses vii-public-v1 and stores rendered navigation responses by request URL.
observations.evidence: Direct read of https://vii.spaplus.co/sw.js showed cache.put(request, response.clone()) and caches.match(request) for navigation.

observations.observation: The cumulative candidate contains an Aurora circuit breaker plus D1 and accepted bundled catalog fallback.
observations.evidence: app/lib/runtime-database.ts and app/lib/public-catalog-read.ts; built-candidate logs showed selected and detail fallback while still returning the business page with HTTP 200.
Source comparison of the Hebrew labels and public browser reproduction.

hypotheses.mechanism: The unversioned service-worker document cache can replay old HTML after a release and pair it with newer hashed assets, reaching the route error boundary.
hypotheses.prediction: The public worker caches navigation documents, while a worker that caches only the offline shell eliminates this cross-release path.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Read the public worker, change navigation handling to network plus offline shell only, and assert no document put or request replay.
hypotheses.result: Supported. The public v1 worker cached full navigation responses. The v2 regression test proves navigation contains no cache.put(request) or caches.match(request).

hypotheses.mechanism: A transient Aurora or catalog-read failure escapes on the currently deployed build and produces a server 500.
hypotheses.prediction: The public business route can fail once and then succeed, while the cumulative candidate renders it when cloud database access is unavailable by using the accepted fallback chain.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Compare fresh public reproduction with the exact built candidate running without cloud bindings.
hypotheses.result: Supported. Production returned a direct intermittent 500. The built candidate logged public catalog fallbacks but rendered the same business route with HTTP 200.

hypotheses.mechanism: A deterministic render or hydration exception exists in the candidate independent of network and release state.
hypotheses.prediction: The same candidate route or viewport fails consistently during repeated local browser checks.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Run home, vacation search, business detail and business reload on desktop and 390 pixel mobile.
hypotheses.result: Rejected. All eight candidate checks returned expected content with no HTTP 500, visible shared error boundary or page exception.

fix.change: Release the cumulative database fallback candidate and prevent release mixing by changing the service worker to cache only release-independent shell assets. Centralize bounded route and global asset recovery so CacheStorage failure cannot block a single reload.
fix.evidence: Targeted tests passed 10 of 10 and the exact built candidate passed eight desktop and mobile route and reload checks with zero failures.

affected_family: business detail vacation-164 cold load and reload
service-worker navigation on desktop and 390 pixel mobile

regression_checks.evidence: tests/pwa-experience.test.mjs asserts v2 shell cache and prohibits navigation document caching or replay.
tests/navigation-unit-results-regression.test.mjs verifies both boundaries use one helper, a 60 second guard, cache cleanup and reload.
qa:route-reliability against http://127.0.0.1:4191 completed eight desktop and mobile checks with zero failures.

remaining_unknowns: The original server digest was not exposed by the public 500 response, so the exact first failing Aurora call cannot be named from production logs.
authorization_boundary: Read-only production diagnosis, local repair and tests, and one explicitly authorized public release; no data, schema, DNS, environment, sharing or permission changes.
